workspace_diagnostics.message: No architecture boundaries are configured, so the boundary detector did not run and its violation counts are zero because nothing was measured. Add `boundaries` to the config, or set `boundary-violation` to off to state that the check is not wanted.

No rule packs are configured, so the policy detector did not run and its violation counts are zero because nothing was measured. Add `rulePacks` to the config, or set `policy-violation` to off to state that the check is not wanted.

metric_interpretation.crap_caveat: CRAP is static estimated coverage risk, not measured coverage or evidence of an uncovered branch.
metric_interpretation.structural_definition: Structural findings exceed cyclomatic and/or cognitive thresholds; CRAP-only findings have exceeded=crap.

summary.test_reference_note: Test references are source links, not execution proof. The final integrated verification is reported as passing tsc, Biome (802 files), build, compiled smoke, and diff checks; no-remote-preflight reports pass 3 and batch 10.

health_records.explanation: Builds one query object from URL parameters: rejects an unresolved priority, canonicalizes each excludeStatus value, resolves parent IDs including bare numeric IDs, returns 404/409 for absent or ambiguous parents, and only disables cross-branch refresh when resolving a parent. Labels merge repeated and comma-delimited parameters before the single query call.
Maps each value-taking completion flag to its provider and restricts task type/project suggestions to command-subcommand combinations that accept them.

Obtains the store, refreshes only a warm cross-branch store when requested, and rechecks both session generation and store identity after each await. An empty query filters the store corpus; a non-empty query transfers only supported task filters to SearchService, de-duplicates IDs, then filters again. These are stale-read and query-policy branches, not separate transactions.

Creates a server with five configured priorities, verifies create/edit/search schemas expose that exact enum case-insensitively, then creates with VERY HIGH and asserts canonical storage as very high.
Verifies default type schema has no default, replaces configuration with Bug/Epic, then asserts case-normalized creation succeeds and Feature is rejected with the configured-values message.
Places an edit caret on an early wrapped description line, inserts text, and asserts both exact string insertion and that the textarea viewport remains before its final wrapped line.
Builds the initial advanced-config draft by preserving persisted values, copying definitionOfDone, and falling back to DEFAULT_INIT_CONFIG.

The server startup transaction exits for an already-running host, derives port/name from config, temporarily switches to bundled assets, restores that directory on start failure, reports EADDRINUSE distinctly, and opens a browser only when both caller and config allow it.
Owns the edit command transaction: chooses wizard versus flags, resolves targets, parses one shared update, applies it, and accumulates per-target failures for batch output.
Normalizes only configured exclude-status, type, project, and priority filters in parallel while preserving raw status semantics and omitting empty filters.

Fails before initialization, applies each optional status, exclusion, type, project, assignee, priority, and parent predicate cumulatively, then returns a copied array. Status sets deliberately support repeated status flags; returning slice() prevents caller mutation of cached state.

Selects a matching contextual task only when IDs agree, rejects branch/draft read-only state, falls back from task lookup to draft lookup, and resolves either an active file or a uniquely identified draft reference. The branches preserve the distinct not-found, ambiguous, unreadable, and identity-conflict results required by the TUI.

Runs git with ignored stdin to avoid MCP stdio deadlock, disables optional locks for reads, drains both output streams, supplies optional input, and on timeout kills the POSIX process group or Windows task tree before rejecting. Non-accepted exit codes retain stderr in the thrown error.

Derives effective statuses from persisted configuration or defaults, adds Draft only when absent, and asserts create/edit schema enum, first-status default, case-insensitivity, and whitespace normalization.
Supplies every prefilled edit field and asserts the wizard converts cleared due date to null, preserves dependency text, rewrites checklist operations, and normalizes each edited scalar/list value.

This is the TUI composition lifecycle, not duplicate state ownership: TaskViewerSession owns corpus/filter/selection state (lines 261-280), TaskViewerRendering owns widgets (486-509), and this function wires their loading, modal, subscription, keyboard, and teardown boundaries. The cognitive threshold alone is not a concrete architectural defect.

Consumes one token only when it is well formed, has a nonempty field/value split, and the field is recognized. It appends repeatable status/priority/assignee values, accumulates labels/types/modified files, validates priority and result type, and deliberately leaves malformed, unknown, and invalid filter tokens in the free-text query.
CLI create orchestration is the owner of choosing interactive input versus flags before delegating construction and persistence to shared task helpers.

Retries if the session, filesystem, git object, or root changes while loading config, fetching refs, or reading the branch snapshot. It locally refreshes on an unchanged fingerprint; otherwise it coalesces one store refresh and reruns when it joined an older refresh. This is the required generation-consistent read policy.

Captures project collaborators, checks them after every asynchronous phase, honors cancellation, loads local and branch corpora, builds the identity index, then compares pre/post branch stability fingerprints. It only publishes shared freshness for the installed corpus and marks partial branch loads stale. The outer method owns the bounded three-attempt retry.

Schedules delayed task/document/decision rechecks, renames all three without changing content, fires rename events and stale timers, then asserts each cached identity follows its new path without regression.
Uses an overlong configured type on a 100-column screen, asserts selector rows stack and widths fit content, then verifies arrow navigation reaches Create and returns through Priority.

Guards unsaved modal edits only for ordinary primary-button navigations. Modified clicks, prevented events, external targets, non-HTTP links, and same-document anchors retain their normal behavior; other navigations require confirmation and are cancelled when the user declines.

Rejects a state unless version, task ID, and sessions array agree; each session must pass isSession, and optional active ID, worktree, successful-session flag, handoff document ID, and handoff payload must have their exact types. mutate validates again before atomically replacing state.json under its lock.

Treats presence of any init configuration flag, including an explicit false value, as a fully specified noninteractive invocation; public init help exposes these as command inputs, and the preexisting CLI integration coverage invokes explicit boolean settings with --defaults.
Validates integration aliases and enforces that MCP or none cannot coexist with agent-file or Claude-agent requests before the wizard starts.

Normalizes required inputs, rejects missing, omitted-moved, and duplicate IDs, resolves all rows from a refreshed store, rejects ambiguity and cross-branch writes, delegates ordinal planning, and persists only changed tasks. These validations prevent silent corruption of caller ordering.

Loads and validates the current store, conditionally refreshes a warm cross-branch corpus, returns found tasks, throws candidate paths for ambiguity, and finally probes the local filesystem to distinguish missing from a superseded session. `undefined` means retry by the caller; `null` is a stable miss.

This is one editor transaction: prepare a writable identity, snapshot content, hand off the terminal, compare post-edit content, stamp updatedDate, then reload and publish. Draft writes take a draft lock and reject a changed file; active writes reload parsed content before store publication. Its failure reasons deliberately preserve UI recovery behavior.
Opens help, shrinks the terminal, asserts popup/help bounds remain on screen and scroll reaches the short viewport maximum, then expands and asserts scroll resets to zero.
Feeds every create wizard prompt and asserts normalized status/type, assignees, labels, checked criteria, DoD additions, references, documentation, and unprefixed dependency tokens.
Resizes a live composer from full to compact geometry and asserts field frames, selector coordinates, action visibility, and navigation hint are recomputed rather than retaining stale layout.

Changes selected task atomically for the workspace: clears prior state only for a new identity, increments generation before async session lookup, restores task scroll positions, and rejects late results after close/reselection.

Maps each editor result reason to a specific footer message; on a saved task it replaces by ID or file path, rerenders, and reports changed versus unchanged. The branches are result-domain handling, not duplicated ownership.

Initializes the header's sole mutable filter state, canonical visible-control order, first width-derived layout, container, and child controls. Each optional input has a distinct default; no transaction is delegated here.

Rejects missing canonical components, blank formats, duplicate or missing yyyy/mm/dd date tokens, and invalid hh/mm time tokens. It performs one-pass token replacement, leaves date-only values date-only, and appends canonical time when the configured format has no time component.

Owns the routed modal session: it keys the editor by session, supplies draft-only status options, creates task/draft records, and handles archive cleanup notices. Session and mount checks prevent delayed create/archive results from changing a newer modal; timers are cleared on unmount and moved archive failures refresh then warn instead of silently retrying.

Rejects drags for cross-branch tasks and temporarily exposes the branch tooltip. For local tasks it serializes task/status/lane transfer data, conditionally joins a modifier-selected card to a batch, builds a bounded stacked drag image for batches, and synchronizes card and board drag state.
Board export action owns loading tasks with progress, README-marker export versus file export, overwrite confirmation, and loading-screen cleanup on errors.
The milestone-resolution continuation combines the already validated scalar and list inputs into the exact Core create-task input shape.

Derives one normalized snapshot key: disabled or filesystem-only operation suppresses branch-history cutoff, while defaults cover activity window, remote policy, prefix, resolution strategy, statuses, and backlog directory. Keeping this together makes snapshot cache identity match branch-load policy.

Skips prohibited modes, rate-limits ordinary fetches, lets forced callers await an existing fetch, coalesces concurrent fetches, logs fetch failures without failing local reads, and only timestamps the same git instance. The promise identity guards against replacement-session state leaks.

The watcher reconciliation captures a generation/version baseline, tolerates transient load failure by scheduling retry, ignores unexpected-ID events, rejects stale root/generation work, merges disk content with concurrent publications, and notifies only when visible, identity, corpus, or config state changed. This is necessary watcher conflict policy.

Normalizes line endings, refuses ambiguous checklist sentinels, retains only marked or checklist-bearing legacy ranges as mutable, removes them right-to-left, then inserts the regenerated section after preferred preceding headings, before following headings, or at EOF. It restores the original CRLF choice on every write path.

The reorder endpoint validates taskId, targetStatus, and a non-empty orderedTaskIds array, preserves the distinct null versus omitted targetMilestone cases, delegates one reorder transaction, and maps ambiguous IDs to 409, expected lookup/input failures to 400, and all other failures to 500.
Spawns debug MCP over pipes, waits for its start message, closes stdin, asserts clean code 0/no signal, and aggregates any primary close and forced-cleanup failures.
Captures prompt metadata for default selections and asserts status defaults to To Do with Draft included, while priority/type use select prompts and retain empty defaults.
Clicks description then title twice and asserts exclusive readInput mode, focus, cursor visibility, border/inverse styles, typed values, Tab traversal, and cancellation without persistence.

Builds a deterministic browser render transaction: derives route/highlight ID, registers only expected fetches, optionally controls health timing, renders under StrictMode, and settles status/search/routed requests in intentional order.

Rejects mouse input while attached/configuring/composing, converts coordinates only inside the tree, then distinguishes header click-to-toggle, hover/select, and task selection without mutating unrelated workspace state.
The Tab binding is a guarded view handoff: it refuses overlays/filter focus, reports the selected task, then closes once before invoking either supplied callback or ViewSwitcher.

Builds milestone buckets from active and archived entities, filters their already-loaded tasks through the shared search index, and partitions them into unassigned, active, and completed groups. It separately tracks expansion, unassigned pagination, completed visibility, drag state, search no-match feedback, and the true empty state so these render modes do not interfere.

Requires a local demotable task, confirmation, and no active request. It serializes demotion, refreshes data and draft listeners after success, reports dependency cleanup, and distinguishes confirmed moved-state, lost network response, refresh failure, and ordinary API failure. Request epoch and active-request checks prevent a stale completion from closing or changing a replacement modal.

For each starting/running session, preserves a starting launch owned by a live PID, probes tmux and pane death otherwise, kills abandoned starting panes, and atomically marks abandoned launches failed or running sessions stopped. It then resolves an orphaned replacement handoff and resumes requested, ready, or failed handoffs.
Parses mutually exclusive assignee state, normalizes configured filters, and records all-label matching in the query request.

Avoids duplicate or stale watchers, normalizes event paths, serializes callback work through the root queue, and on rename adds a watcher only for a confirmed new directory or removes the vanished subtree. These branches implement recursive watching on platforms without native recursive support.

Moves an installed target into a private recovery directory before inspecting ownership. It deletes only when the recovered inode identity is transaction-owned; failed moves, reads, removal, or directory cleanup return explicit preservation evidence. This is intentionally conservative rollback, not removable complexity.

Inside the vacated-reference lock it reloads the task, rejects terminal status, verifies source and destination paths, moves the file, publishes the transition, cleans references, and optionally stages/commits all affected files. Failures after the move are marked so recovery knows filesystem state already changed.

Preserves deterministic identifier precedence: numeric inputs prefer raw then canonical IDs, while textual inputs prefer raw ID then a unique title. Alias, variant ID, and variant title paths require uniqueness where ambiguity is possible, so a lookup never guesses between multiple title matches.

Returns no ranges for ambiguous sentinels; otherwise derives marked bodies from balanced target pairs, masks foreign sentinel ranges, and records whether each body contains checklist items. Legacy headings are considered only when no attached marked range exists or the caller explicitly needs both, avoiding stray marker pairs hiding legacy data.

Delegates the atomic rename/update workflow, returns an explicit no-change result, and otherwise reports title, due-date, skipped task update, updated local IDs, and physical file move independently. MilestoneWorkflowError is converted to the MCP tool error preserving its code.

The init route validates parsed input and rejects an already initialized project before calling initializeProject; it constrains source/location enums, normalizes optional arrays and booleans, notifies services only after success, and returns parsed failure text as a 500 response.

Configures Web/API projects, verifies project schema enum and case normalization, then asserts create detail, persisted project, list badges, and later edit/view behavior for projected and unprojected tasks.

This promise closure is the board composition root. It owns local projections, popup/modal flags, bindings, watcher updates, write settlement, rendering, and teardown for exactly one board screen lifetime.

Serializes one board filter popup and routes each filter kind to its distinct picker shape. A non-null result updates only its filter fields, emits copied state, rerenders, then reliably restores focus.

Confirms a recruited move by snapshotting the projected order before awaits, skipping unavailable/no-op targets, persisting batch status/order, merging all changed tasks, and always settling the pending write.

Walks only an active, writable move's recruitment cursor. It reanchors collapsed-set insertion coordinates, inserts the ghost row, skips the grabbed task, bounds movement, then updates highlight and render.
Normalizes one Blessed event into deduplicated modifier/name candidates: it prefers explicit ctrl/shift/meta construction, retains a meaningful full name, and avoids adding an unmodified duplicate.

Maps configured browser shortcuts to suggestion navigation, committing the selected suggestion only with nonblank input, removing the final chip only from an empty input, and dismissing suggestions. Disabled inputs are inert; modulo arithmetic keeps keyboard selection within the current suggestion list.

Resolves selected IDs against current tasks, preserves status-column ordering for resolvable tasks while retaining stale IDs for server reporting, and skips a no-op status/milestone move after alias canonicalization. It clears selection before the request, surfaces partial failures, applies returned changed tasks when possible, otherwise refreshes, and reports request errors.

Refuses comments while demoting, for absent/cross-branch tasks, or with blank bodies. It rejects standalone YAML delimiters in body or author before appending, preserves edit mode across the ensuing refresh, updates local comments and clears inputs on success, and only mutates error/loading state for the current modal epoch.

Constructs the task endpoint query from only supplied filters, preserves repeatable exclusion and label values through the shared encoder, and defaults cross-branch loading on to match the TUI unless explicitly disabled. It delegates JSON/error/retry behavior to the client transport rather than duplicating it.

Claims a requested handoff under the session-state lock only if IDs/status match and no dispatch owner is alive. It then rechecks state, verifies a running session and stable empty input before pasting, records waiting state otherwise, records dispatchedAt after send, and clears only its own owner PID in finally.
List execution coordinates duplicate-ID protection, request parsing, interactive projection, JSON paging, grouped text rendering, and disposal of search/content stores.
Updates one selected preset immutably after rejecting env-clear conflicts, absent presets, invalid bootstrap values, and invalid worktree booleans.
Serializes behavior configuration with deliberate display defaults, including disabled padding and immutable taskPrefix.
Renders the post-wizard summary from merged settings and separates completion success, failure, and skip states.
Uses supplied name first, otherwise requires a TTY, validates a new name, and allows a reinitialization to retain its configured name.
Owns storage selection because it validates directory/location combinations, bypasses storage changes on reinit, and selects prompt versus deterministic defaults.
Produces the unified-view label from the same optional query/status/type/project/priority/file filters passed to that view.

Creates at most one SearchService for the currently verified ContentStore, retries instead of exposing a service if root/session/store identity changes during either initialization, and rethrows only initialization failures belonging to the current objects. It is a generation-safe cache facade.

Loads config state first, treats unreadable legacy text as no legacy milestones, migrates schema only when required, creates only nonempty legacy titles absent by ID or title key, saves only when content changed, then performs draft-prefix migration. Ordering prevents duplicate milestone creation and migration against unloaded configuration.

Preserves unmoved rows verbatim, groups consecutive moved rows, computes each group between its actual neighboring rows, carries the rebalance requirement, and applies status/milestone movement with the allocated ordinal per offset. This is the minimal algorithm for multiple discontiguous moved blocks.

Requires initialized state, normalizes empty query/type defaults, compiles the task matcher once, uses non-fuzzy collection filtering for blank searches, otherwise filters Fuse hits by requested type and task filters before applying the result limit. The limit after filtering is essential.

Pins eligible refs, reports remote/local progress separately, indexes each ref through a bounded four-worker queue, preserves incomplete status from any failed index, and chooses hydration candidates differently when local tasks exist. Separate remote and local identity maps avoid conflating source precedence.

Computes the write target, preserves an existing serialized ID and parent ID when identities compare equal, otherwise normalizes both, removes same-ID files only for a newly-derived path, writes after ensuring the directory, then publishes one task content mutation with root, ID, and path.

Builds optional metadata lines in display order while preserving required Created. It independently handles normalized priority/assignee/reporter and conditional ordinal, dates, labels, milestone fields.
Renders parent identity, either detailed or count-only subtasks, references, and documentation. The subtask-summary fallback avoids inventing task titles when the detail query did not load them.

Before every attempt, verifies the task working hash, stages only the requested path, captures its index entries, and commits the selected path. On retry it refuses if either working content or index entries changed; otherwise it backs off and reports the final operation failure after the bounded attempt count.

Preserves empty values, distinguishes UTC-midnight Date objects as date-only, emits minute precision for timed Dates, strips scalar quotes, and handles canonical space-separated and ISO T-separated date-times before subsequent date parsing. The branch order prevents a date-time from being reduced to a date.

FakeTmux records every command and deliberately branches for prepare failure, pane launch failure, Git worktree detection, capture failure, and pane listing so session tests exercise durable recovery paths.
Exercises a multi-task status move with ordering/failure outcomes and asserts the returned moved/changed task sets and persisted ordinals reflect the transactional projection.
Asserts the board control hierarchy rather than only text: toolbar placement, heading/new-task relationship, filter container, selector ARIA labels, and concrete responsive/control classes.

Handles single-task move confirmation: collapse an active recruitment preview first, delegate sets, cancel true no-ops, snapshot order before I/O, persist reorder, merge changed tasks, and settle on success or error.
Creates an owned screen only when no parent exists, merges explicit style with interaction defaults, constructs a non-native-key list, then initializes rendered mappings, handlers, and selected item.

Registers all list interaction policy in one place: boundary-aware arrows, paging, mapped selection, multi-select, search editing, and cancel. Each handler mutates the same list selection/search state.

Produces the initialization review rows from wizard state: mode label, config path, and base project fields are always shown; MCP clients, CLI agent-file count, Claude installation, and a normalized task prefix appear only when their corresponding mode/options apply. This is presentation-specific conditional disclosure, not duplicated initialization logic.

Submits the wizard's selected initialization contract: custom paths are normalized when valid while invalid text remains available for validation feedback, MCP and CLI payload fields are mutually scoped to their modes, and advanced settings omit falsy optional overrides. It reports initialization failures locally and calls the supplied initialized transition only after the API resolves.

Rejects unsafe preset property names, non-object presets, empty or NUL-bearing commands, NUL-bearing prepare strings, non-boolean worktree flags, and unsupported bootstrap values before validating every environment key/value pair.
Archive/complete action shares local-editability enforcement, then branches only for archive dependency cleanup versus terminal-status completion.
Derives implied result types from task-only filters, rejects incompatible explicit types, resolves filters, and validates the positive limit.
Parses scalar task mutations while enforcing ordinal, milestone, and due-date conflicts before list/content assembly.

The create lock encloses parent resolution, ID allocation, dependency validation, ordinal selection, target/previous content capture, and the write. Finalization occurs afterward; any failure restores only matching generated index/file state and explicitly preserves externally changed state. This directly protects old-root allocation races.

Builds the exact persisted semantic projection used for updatedDate policy: it includes every editable scalar, collection, structured section, comments, and status callback while normalizing optional arrays/content. It intentionally excludes filesystem metadata and updatedDate itself so saveTask preserves timestamps for no-op writes.

Normalizes CRLF and trims bodies, rejects empty additions, collapses author whitespace, preserves supplied createdDate, and rejects comment markers or standalone frontmatter delimiters in all persisted comment fields. Those checks prevent a comment from changing Markdown structure.

Normalizes the requested identifier and candidate keys, skips README and malformed files, classifies every parsed milestone into raw/canonical/alias/title/variant buckets, then delegates ambiguity-safe precedence to chooseMatch. Read failures cannot convert into a false positive match.

Only rewrites bare due_date mapping lines; it retains indentation and trailing comments, leaves null and already quoted values untouched, and quotes a bare scalar while escaping backslashes and double quotes so YAML cannot coerce the written calendar value.

The update endpoint parses the patch before mutation, resolves string milestones, keeps draft and task update paths distinct, and includes demotion recovery state when present. It maps ambiguous IDs and task/create locks to 409 while preserving malformed update input as 400.

Checks only supplied optional fields and returns the first precise error: blank/non-string title, non-string/non-null path, non-string type, or a tags value that is not an all-string array. parseDocumentUpdate separately requires content before constructing normalized input.
Recruits TASK-3, asserts first Enter only collapses preview and leaves ordinal unchanged, then second Enter persists adjacent TASK-1/TASK-3 order while retaining To Do status.

Creates TASK-6 with assignee, labels, dependencies, and raw content; demotes it to a newly allocated draft, promotes it again, and asserts every listed field and raw content survive both lifecycle transitions.
Verifies backspace/delete/Ctrl-W at real caret positions across title and description, including astral code points and newline joins, while asserting repaint and cancellation behavior.
Selects the history or active session, emits precise empty-state copy, awaits preview output, and writes only if the workspace remains open, generation matches, and task identity is unchanged.
Rejects equal task/status updates, refreshes source collections and derived filter options, defers render during creation, otherwise projects the board and synchronizes an open popup.
Chooses highlighted or nearest unrecruited non-branch neighbor, reports no candidate/branch denial, toggles selected IDs through insertion-index preservation, and rerenders the projected move.
Guards invalid indices, restores prior row styling, prevents select-event recursion during programmatic selection, updates mapped display content, emits highlight once, and optionally renders.
Produces workflow-only metadata descriptors: project only under configured projects, milestone through optional alias resolver, parent with optional title, and pluralized subtask count.

Suppresses an empty unassigned section outside search, removes completed tasks, orders remaining work by newest creation date, and caps the default display at twelve. It renders search-sensitive empty copy, expansion and show-all controls, and forwards edit/drag behavior for each displayed row.

Optimistically changes exactly one Definition of Done item and sends the server's check or uncheck operation rather than rewriting the whole list. Per-field request counters plus task identity ensure only the latest request for the current task can roll back state, report an error, or trigger refresh.

For unsaved tasks it updates form state only; for persisted tasks it prevents concurrent type requests, optimistically sets the type, adopts the canonical type returned by the server, and rolls back only if that request remains current for the same task. Type-specific loading/error state is intentionally separate from generic inline updates.

The lifecycle effect recognizes a refresh of the same open task versus a new modal session. It re-syncs form data while preserving dirty fields on refresh, preserves edit mode after comment refresh when requested, otherwise selects create or preview mode, clears transient comment/error state, and updates prior-modal refs.

Requires an object configuration, a safe selectedPreset name, an object presets map containing that selected name, then validates every named preset. This makes selection validity and each executable preset's shape a single load-time invariant.

Rejects non-records, a foreign task ID, unknown status, missing required strings, invalid preset snapshots/config scope, incorrectly typed optional terminal fields, and non-numeric owner PIDs. The predicate is the gate used before durable session state is returned or rewritten.

Requires one of five handoff states and required ID/session/document path/timestamp strings, permits optional dispatch/replacement PIDs only as numbers, and if an embedded document exists validates its required scalar fields and optional string tags.
Interactive editing owns candidate selection, target resolution, config-backed wizard choices, cancellation, and formatted update errors.
Applies noninteractive overrides with the required dependency that disabling branch checks also disables remote operations.
The initialization workflow must sequence cwd/git/config/name/storage/prefix/integration/advanced selection before one initializeProject call and outcome reporting.
Reports completion-install outcome and CLI-integration artifacts while intentionally suppressing agent-file output for MCP and none modes.
Validates the requested port, finds a fallback, and makes the fallback automatic only for noninteractive callers while letting interactive users abort.
Maps replacement and append flags for task text sections, retaining repeated values and the independent final-summary clear signal.
Completes a list request with validated limit, nonblank canonicalized parent display ID, sort validation, trimmed search, and readiness intent.

Loads active, completed, and config concurrently against one filesystem/root snapshot; if either identity changes, discards supplied active tasks and retries. It then builds the index with working-copy-only branch context and only returns after a second stability check.

Rejects publications lacking an owned/current root, avoids unchanged writes, advances item generation/version before publication, queues non-published-root writes, and selects branch versus working-copy publication only when an identity index exists. These guards stop stale roots and watcher reloads from overwriting newer state.

Decision watcher work verifies publication ownership and item generation both before and after disk I/O, schedules retry on read failure/invalid identity, suppresses unchanged decisions, then versions, sorts, caches, and notifies only initialized stores. This mirrors the store's stale-event policy.

Parses only a scalar top-level id line, retains matching quote style and trailing comment, canonical-compares the existing value to the planned old ID, and replaces exactly that span. Refusing malformed or mismatched content is required to avoid destructive repair.

Normalizes both names, resolves the active source, preserves/clears/validates due date according to undefined/null/value input, detects alias conflicts only for title changes, and records whether task references should change. It separates validation from the later mutation/rollback transaction.

Requires an existing document, rejects an explicit blank title, normalizes ID/type/tags, sets updatedDate, preserves the old subpath only when no new path was supplied, writes through the shared createDocument path, then returns reloaded state. These branches define patch semantics.

Applies replacement only after validation, appends validated IDs without duplicates, removes by canonical ID equality, and writes the final dependency array even when empty. Invalid dependencies fail before assignment, so callers cannot persist a partially updated collection.

Clear precedes replacement and append; final summary clears to an empty string while optional plan/notes fields are removed. Appends trim empty values and use a double-newline separator. It reports mutation only for an actual clear/replacement/usable append.

Selects the last top-level occurrence when available, otherwise the last indented occurrence, then collects through its nested block until the next mapping at equal-or-less indentation. That isolates a key from unrelated malformed YAML while keeping multiline YAML values intact.

For each bounded HEAD-update attempt, creates a commit from the prepared temporary index, restores each owned index path only if its current entries still match, then updates HEAD with the expected base ref. A concurrent index change aborts rather than overwriting unrelated staging.

Sorts a copy of criteria by index, replaces only unmasked checklist lines in the existing body one-for-one, preserves prose and masked foreign content, trims outer blank lines, and appends remaining criteria with one separating blank line when preceding prose requires it.

Walks metadata lines, ignores non key-value syntax, accepts only positive finite index values, normalizes author whitespace, and preserves a trimmed created value. Callers reindex parsed comments, so malformed or duplicate indexes cannot destabilize stored order.

Normalizes body line endings and whitespace, rejects section markers and standalone delimiters in body, author, and created date, emits author/created only when present, and always frames the body with canonical --- delimiters that the parser consumes.

Recognizes HTML block type 1 tags, comments, processing instructions, declarations, and CDATA, returning no state when the matching closer is on the same line and otherwise returning the exact closer regex. It intentionally leaves blank-line HTML block types to the adjacent matcher.

Reserves ID aliases from active and archived milestones, counts active title keys, then exposes active IDs plus only titles that are unique and do not collide with any reserved ID. The resulting set correctly separates configured milestones from task-only values.

Classifies malformed JSON/object bodies as 400, MilestoneWorkflowError NOT_FOUND as 404 and VALIDATION_ERROR as 400, defaults other failures to 500, logs only 500s, and emits a stable code alongside the error message.
Moves an In Progress task into To Do, recruits TASK-1, captures the collapsed preview, persists it, and asserts saved ordinals exactly match the previewed order.
Creates TASK-1 locally, pushes it, changes its status to Done on feature, fetches remote branches after returning main, and verifies remote branch task data is available for board status merging.

Renames target task/document/decision while corrupting siblings, asserts target identities relocate without delayed rechecks, then deletes targets and asserts only targets disappear while malformed siblings remain.
Exhausts an old retry budget, sends a fresh same-key event and asserts fresh retries complete, then storms 100 duplicate events and asserts one deferred entry with bounded reads/timers.
Connects a real stdio MCP client, verifies document_create remains listed after listTools, then performs document creation under per-operation timeouts and aggregates cleanup errors.
Exercises draft-edit interaction branches and asserts the draft remains on its draft lifecycle path while edit outcomes and TUI cleanup are handled correctly.

Inserts astral characters mid-title and description, asserts terminal-column cursors and persisted YAML/Markdown contain whole code points, then reloads canonical task values without surrogate corruption.
Resolves a named deferred fetch exactly once with status/payload controls so tests can order stale and fresh browser refresh responses before asserting rendered state.
Converts a Blessed mouse point to a task-tree row only when layout and coordinates are present and strictly within its content rectangle; incorporates childBase or scroll offset.
Commits the current editor widget into the selected task's draft, including cursor/scroll restoration data, then cancels/destroys the widget and returns focus to refreshed details.
The Enter binding first rejects blocked focus, confirms move mode through the move transaction, otherwise validates current column/row/task and opens exactly that popup.

Owns one unified TUI lifecycle: keeps stdin alive, loads initial corpus/config, handles empty policy, creates shared session/screen/watchers, publishes updates, and releases watchers/listeners on exit.

Applies key-specific lexical checks: bracket arrays, definition_of_done consistency with parsed config, non-empty project/date strings, boolean literals, bounded safe integers, and alphabetic task prefixes. Unrecognized keys do not invalidate a watched configuration.

Implements the dialog Tab boundary: an empty dialog focuses itself, focus arriving from outside enters at the appropriate end, Shift+Tab wraps from first/dialog to last, and Tab wraps last to first. Non-Tab keys are intentionally left for modal shortcut handling.

Bridges one board card to column reordering. Drag-over is ignored unless reordering is enabled and the drag is not a selected multi-card batch; self drops get a distinct state, other drops compute before/after from pointer position, and visual insertion markers reflect that state around the card.

Shows a readiness badge only when readiness is meaningful, dependencies exist, and the form's dependency list and status still exactly match the persisted task. Hiding it while edits diverge prevents a stale readiness claim during unsaved changes.

Rejects duplicate removal and missing milestone selection, requires a reassignment target when requested, then removes with either clear or reassign semantics. It coordinates loading, feedback clearing/success text, refresh, dialog reset, and recoverable error state in the one milestone-removal workflow.

Optimistically replaces the checked value of the addressed acceptance criterion, persists the complete criteria list, refreshes after success, and conditionally restores its snapshot on failure. The current task identity and per-field sequence protect a later toggle or modal change from stale rollback.

Runs a bounded attempt loop with configured or explicit retry count. It immediately rethrows client-side API errors, exponentially backs off transient/network/server failures, preserves a terminal API error, and wraps exhausted non-API failures as a NetworkError with attempt context.
Consumes benchmark-only argv sequentially, assigns six bounded options, prints help as a null sentinel, and rejects unknown flags. It is a CLI parser, not production task policy.

Temporary Bun.spawn wrapper classifies only array/object command shapes, counts Git processes and rev-parse repository checks, delegates exactly once, and exposes restoration to prevent benchmark instrumentation leakage.

The startReserved state mutation rejects a conflicting replacement or any starting/running session, constructs one starting session with a stable task worktree path and owner PID, appends it, and claims activeSessionId. Expensive work runs after the lock; failure atomically marks that reservation failed and clears the active claim.
Formats one Markdown board row across ordered columns, yielding empty cells for absent/incomplete tasks and otherwise composing depth prefix, ID/title, normalized assignees, and labels.
Applies only the preview fingerprint, prints every rename and reference warning, then rechecks dependency defects and preserves nonrepairable findings as failures.
Chooses text fallback when no usable tasks exist; otherwise opens the unified list with either file-filtered search tasks or the complete local task set.
Resolves a parent identity once, queries local tasks, loads readiness details only when requested, then applies shared sorting, child narrowing, and limit to text and JSON rows.
Adapts both custom text prompts and Clack selects to TaskWizardQuestion, including empty-backspace previous-field navigation and cancellation conversion.
Creates the editable wizard snapshot by converting task lists/checklists to prompt text and supplying empty defaults for absent fields.

Creates one store lazily, initializes it, retries if initialization belonged to a superseded root/session/store, throws disposal immediately, and returns only after a final identity check. The loop is required because project switching can occur during initialization.

Resolves a deduplicated requested set and records ambiguity, missing, and cross-branch failures per task rather than discarding the batch. It then applies status/milestone policy, chooses explicit-order or append placement, and returns both moved and actually changed tasks for one later bulk write.

Merges placement and conflict-resolution updates by task ID, preserves original state for both ordered and moved inputs, derives moved task output, and persists only status, ordinal, or milestone changes. In particular it does not treat an ordinal-only plan as an unrelated edit.

Validates removal policy first, updates task references unless keeping them, rolls those updates back if archive fails, archives before committing, and rolls back archive plus task changes if commit fails. It returns a structured result only after both filesystem and optional Git transaction complete.

Restores a missing original using exclusive creation, refuses an externally replaced file, and otherwise removes/restores only when current bytes equal the transaction-created bytes and Git index restoration succeeded. This exact-content policy prevents rollback from deleting another writer's result.

Converts absolute paths relative to the appropriate worktree/repository root, normalizes separators, prefixes project-relative backlog paths only when needed, and collapses completed/archive lifecycle paths to their task identity. The branches make equivalent paths collide rather than appear as separate tasks.

Orders candidate records by working-copy preference, optional most-progressed configured-status rank, modification time, and deterministic record key. This comparator is the documented resolution policy; the final key ensures stable output for ties.

Sorts identities by normalized path, selects one lifecycle record per identity, excludes archived and optionally completed records, selects the preferred task version within that lifecycle, and annotates completed output. It intentionally does not merge competing identities, allowing ambiguity detection elsewhere.

Normalizes assignee, reloads the original to detect status and semantic changes, sets/preserves/removes updatedDate accordingly, saves, publishes the active task, optionally commits, then runs the callback only after the write. This order is necessary for timestamp/status output and callback observers to see persisted state.

Selects task-local callback over config callback, skips absent commands, passes old/new status, ID, title, and project cwd, reports failed callback output to stderr, prints successful output only under DEBUG, and never converts callback failure into a failed persisted mutation.

Processes replacement, then unique additions, then removals against the evolving list. The optional key makes labels case-insensitive while references/documentation remain exact; each assignment occurs only when arrays differ. This ordering is the public update-input contract.

Clones existing comments, starts new indexes after the current maximum, captures one fallback timestamp per batch, sanitizes each requested input, preserves valid supplied author/date, and assigns the cloned list only when at least one comment was accepted. This avoids shared-array mutation and index reuse.

Loads editor config, directly invokes the editor without a screen, or leaves Blessed, restores terminal cursor/keypad mode, pauses input, and guarantees resume/re-enter/keypad/render in finally. The terminal-state branches are mandatory for both editor success and failure.

Scans character-by-character only inside double-quoted YAML scalars, preserves single-quoted content, counts each backslash run, avoids escaping the closing quote when odd slashes already preserve it, and returns undefined when no repair was needed.

Normalizes the document ID and subpath, chooses the canonical filename, renames an existing source when it moved, removes other same-ID matches, writes serialized content, and sets document.path only after the write. ENOENT during a rename is tolerated because the source disappeared; other rename failures propagate.

Rollback restores a moved target to its source and rewrites original content when both paths differ; otherwise it rewrites original content at whichever path exists. It intentionally suppresses rollback failure to preserve the initiating mutation error.

Parses the NUL-delimited --raw log as timestamp groups, stops on malformed timestamps, records the first (newest) modification date per path, and reads two paths for rename/copy status records rather than treating their second path as a later commit.

Finds the destination repository context, exits without staging when it is not a repository, derives both paths relative to that repository, tolerates an already-absent source during git add --all, always stages the destination, and returns a non-root repository for later commit selection.

Only preprocesses assignee/reporter mappings, delegates bracketed flow-list handling first, then quotes a bare scalar while preserving already bracketed, quoted, or block-list syntax. This confines YAML coercion protection to identity fields.

Special-cases checklist sections through their parsed range ends, resolves known sentinel ranges before comments or structured blocks, and only falls back to a legacy regex outside masked ranges. It returns undefined rather than inserting relative to an ambiguous or absent section.

Mirrors end lookup for insertion-before operations: checklist ranges first, then sentinel comments/structured blocks outside known masked ranges, then legacy headings outside those ranges. This keeps structural insertions from targeting marker text embedded in other sections.

The create-document route derives a title from filename only when title is absent, rejects a blank result, passes content/type/path/tags through their parsing boundaries, returns 201 on success, maps payload/type/path validation failures to 400, and hides unexpected server errors behind 500.

The milestone update route validates title and due-date semantics, preserves omitted versus explicit dueDate clearing, defaults updateTasks to true, runs one MilestoneWorkflow rename, broadcasts only after success, and delegates error status/code selection to fail.

The statistics route records whether services were already ready, loads the shared store/config, ensures its config watcher, refreshes tasks only after readiness, selects identity-index tasks when present, and serializes Map counts to JSON objects. It returns 500 only if that whole read transaction fails.

The create route rejects an empty title and invalid due date before creation, resolves a string milestone, normalizes checklist/default-DOD fields, returns the created task as 201, and treats allocation lock contention as 409 rather than an ordinary client validation failure.

The demote route delegates one core demotion transaction, returns moved cleanup data on success, publishes only when an error carries partial demotion state, exposes that state and failure cause to support recovery, and maps lock/ambiguity contention to 409.

The bulk move route filters taskIds to strings, distinguishes null from omitted targetMilestone, requires IDs and status, delegates a single move transaction, and returns both moved tasks and per-task failures instead of discarding partial results.
Optional real-tmux test writes a shell agent, waits for its prompt and handoff completion, and asserts the durable handoff reaches ready or completed without replacing the prompt.
Creates TASK-8 with assignee, labels, dependencies, and raw content, edits title/status, then asserts uppercase ID, preserved original fields, retained creation date, and refreshed updated date.
Drives config watcher events through its fixture and asserts update callbacks observe the intended changed configuration while cleanup stops further notifications.
Schedules three targeted delayed writes, injects unrelated wildcard/no-op watcher events, writes all entities, triggers timers, and asserts each changed cached property becomes visible.
Renames entities, initially writes malformed moved files, captures deferred callbacks, restores content, and verifies retrying one watcher observation publishes the recovered identities.
Exercises enhanced initialization choices and asserts the created project configuration/files reflect selected integration and advanced setup values.
Seeds non-init-managed fields including DoD, assignee/reporter, date option, status hook, and MCP HTTP settings, reinitializes, and asserts those unrelated fields remain preserved.
Asserts create dueDate schema is string, edit permits string/null and documents clearing; creates and lists a dated task, clears it, then rejects non-YYYY-MM-DD input.
Joins description lines using Delete at first-line end and Backspace at second-line start after stale cursor offsets, asserting exact joined text and safe cancellation.
Checks an editor's first writable row falls within the scrolling form viewport and that read mode, cursor, and terminal cursor visibility are active for compact-height regressions.
Applies active/inactive visual state to one column: inverse/bold versus move cyan styling, border color, and plain/rich selected-row synchronization. It has no selection ownership beyond display.
Rejects blocked/out-of-range focus, deactivates prior lane, clamps preferred row to target tasks, focuses/activates target, informs board focus owner, and avoids nested renders during projection.

Routes left/right based on mode: ordinary mode focuses adjacent lane; move mode rejects pending/collapsed highlight, derives legal target status/index through policy, updates operation, and projects render.
Opens one selector popup for the active composer field, preserves its current value, applies only non-null selections, restores field focus, and protects composer state from picker cancellation.
Computes one boolean from every normalized filter dimension plus ready and limit flags; this decides initial list selection behavior and intentionally distinguishes limit zero from absent limit.
Escape is a focus-state transition: it ignores overlays, returns filter focus to remembered list/detail pane, returns detail to list, or disposes content/header and exits only from list.

Scans non-comment config lines, rejects a recognized key without a colon, ignores unknown keys, and applies hasValidConfigValue to each recognized explicit scalar. default_assignee deliberately relies on the parsed config because it supports scalar and block sequence forms not represented by this lexical check.

The filesystem callback accepts only change/rename, safely converts a possibly non-string filename, schedules full directory reconciliation for absent, malformed, non-prefixed, or non-Markdown names, and otherwise schedules just the parsed task ID. The watcher error handler is diagnostic-only and stop invalidates pending generations before closing.

Combines task-card rendering with selection and drag semantics: modifier clicks select local cards, normal clicks open details, keyboard shortcuts select or activate, foreign-branch cards are visibly and behaviorally non-draggable, and accessibility text includes acceptance progress when present.

Renders the overview record for a detail/create modal: create-only title entry, description and hierarchy, editable local-only references/files, read-only documentation, acceptance and Definition of Done controls, and a dependency graph only when it has relationships. The branches implement mode, locality, and data-presence policy for this single overview surface.

Keeps dependency-chip navigation in the current board or task-list surface, retains that surface's search string, replaces an existing detail route rather than growing history, and preserves or establishes taskModalFrom for the close destination. Non-board/list locations intentionally fall back to tasks.

The filter effect resets to locally sorted tasks with no filters, filters locally for milestone-only selection including archived-milestone hiding, and otherwise queries the search endpoint for server-backed filters before applying the milestone rule and sort. Its cancellation flag prevents a superseded result or failure from overwriting current display state.

Owns form submission for one milestone: it prevents browser submission, requires a selected nonblank name, rejects title/ID duplicates excluding the edited entity, respects form re-entry protection, persists name and nullable due date, refreshes, and selects accurate update versus rename feedback.

Optimistically applies a multi-field inline metadata update while taking a per-field snapshot and request generation. Milestones normalize null to the empty form value; persistence is skipped for a disabled control or absent task; a failure rolls back only fields whose request remains latest for the same task.

Creates the exact update contract from form state: trims title and optional fields, distinguishes unset priority/milestone/date from explicit values, preserves existing-task null due-date clearing, emits type/project only on creation, omits an empty create assignee when no default exists, then delegates Definition of Done payload choice to the shared policy.

Captures modal keys and gives edit cancel/save precedence. Outside edit mode it ignores editable controls before allowing preview edit or final-status completion shortcuts; every handled shortcut prevents default and propagation, and cleanup removes the capture listener.

Coordinates scoped app refreshes. It escalates to full load before initial success/on load error or when a full request is pending, records a request ID and scope rank, delegates the task/milestone refresh with current-state accessors, discards stale results through the callback, and falls back to full reload only for the current failed request.

Test helper walks one expected folder chain and asserts each node's name, cumulative path, leaf-only document count, child count, and continuation. Its loop is necessary to verify arbitrary nesting without duplicating assertions; it is exercised by the deep-path docs-tree case in the same test file.
Selects the semantic task fields used for benchmark result parity and canonicalizes optional/null and unordered labels/dependencies before digesting; it intentionally omits render-only fields.
Handoff dispatch polling owns the worker-only retry loop and exits on nonrequested, already dispatched, stopped-session, sent, or nonworker states.
Derives storage source and config location deterministically and rejects the invalid custom-directory/folder-config pairing.
Prompts only for new interactive projects, then validates supplied or blank task prefixes through the shared prefix rule.
Builds one result note from persisted config plus selected storage, integration, completion, and filesystem-only state.
Converts six indexed checklist operations with parse-error formatting, then applies replacement, additions, and DoD additions in their distinct fields.
Rejects clear-versus-replace/incremental and replace-versus-incremental acceptance-criteria combinations before any task mutation.
Unified-view loader fetches config and prefiltered local tasks, resolves the parent, sorts children, and adds unfiltered readiness tasks only when display filters require them.

Owns a single status/lane column's local drag, reorder-menu, and selection presentation. It permits ordering only for a multi-task all-local column, computes priority/created-date order, cleans transient drag state on leave/end, delegates drops and range selection to its controller, and conditionally renders status-change target, empty, and terminal cleanup affordances.

Accumulates all benchmark correctness violations before throwing: count, duplicate IDs, missing/unexpected IDs, required sentinels, and forbidden sentinels. This is diagnostic aggregation, not a production path.
Classifies malformed marker and index failures into actionable task-or-draft-specific recovery guidance while preserving unrelated error messages verbatim.
Demote action resolves a local task, performs the transition, reports cleaned dependency links, and converts missing or failed demotions to one local-lookup error.
Scans only the mcp start argument suffix and accepts both separated and equals-form --cwd values before migration chooses a root.
Agents action is the command boundary that requires --update-instructions, prompts for target files, and delegates the managed-block update after project validation.
Doctor execution enforces --yes semantics, renders a diagnosis before any repair, gates repairability and confirmation, and centralizes command failure reporting.
Interactive storage prompting branches between fixed backlog locations with a config-location choice and validated custom paths forced to root config.
Selects CLI overrides or wizard configuration, then overrides every Git-dependent setting for filesystem-only projects.
Provides the shared invariant for list setters: a clear flag cannot accompany values, and blank input is either rejected or interpreted as clear according to the caller.
Rejects clear-labels mixed with any setter and replacement labels mixed with incremental add/remove operations.
Draft list action validates sort fields, resolves output mode, sorts persisted drafts, and selects plain paging versus the unified list view.
Milestone list renderer derives active/completed section visibility from the page window so headers remain truthful across pagination.
Task shorthand action rejects known subcommands, prints help for an omitted ID, and otherwise reuses the local task-view output path before launching detail UI.
Owns interactive advanced configuration because it verifies initialization, runs the wizard, isolates optional completion failure, installs Claude only when selected, and reports all outcomes.
Validates document-search limit as an integer in the command-specific 1..100 range and signals command failure without throwing.
Defines doctor failure as the union of reserved prefixes, local/cross-branch duplicates, content/draft identity issues, self-dependencies, and cycles.
Owns retry semantics for a cancelled-or-failed interactive integration selection while retaining an explicitly requested mode for its first attempt.
Uses explicit aliases or CLI defaults noninteractively, otherwise loops until the interactive selection passes processAgentSelection requirements.
Confirms optional advanced setup, returns defaults on decline, invokes the wizard on acceptance, and records completion-install failure without discarding configuration.
MCP start action resolves explicit versus inferred cwd, sets server pinning accordingly, starts stdio transport, installs shutdown handlers, and preserves config errors verbatim.
Search execution owns duplicate-ID JSON protection, service acquisition, option parsing, interactive/plain/JSON branching, and both service disposals in finally.
Validates clearable task list flags and reference replacement conflicts before translating labels, assignees, dependencies, refs, docs, and modified files into edit args.
Adapts parsed list state and raw Commander fields into unified-view filter arrays, labels, title, description, parent, limit, and readiness fields.
Formats one health subsection with tagged/plain heading and detail, task rows with a supplied color, or a green empty message; callers supply stale and blocked policies separately.

Builds an isolated Git corpus: initializes local/bare repos, writes active/completed tasks, creates branch variants and branch-only tasks, then returns per-surface exact/required/forbidden ID expectations.
Draft viewing loads the canonical draft once, chooses plain versus detail UI, and converts ambiguous identity errors into a command failure.
Loads tasks, active/archived milestones, and config together, builds archival-aware buckets, and formats paginated active and optional completed sections.
Draft target resolution treats selected paths as trusted only when they are direct children of draftsDir and match their canonical reference, preventing a stale or arbitrary path update.
Resolves every requested ID while deduplicating canonical loaded tasks and retaining not-found or ambiguity messages for a complete batch result.
Finds a task file from the loaded task or fallback lookup before completion, returning the exact old/new paths needed for optional Git staging.
Stages only successful non-autocommit repository moves and warns per failed stage rather than falsely reporting the cleanup itself as failed.
Serializes project identity, task defaults, configured collections, milestone IDs, and display settings for config list output.
numericSetter closure performs shared integer/minimum validation before assigning a numeric configuration field.
Dispatches config writes by special editor/filesystem modes, boolean keys, typed setters, and explicit rejected-key guidance.
Formats document-only search rows with path, type, tags, optional score, and the exact doc view follow-up command.
Document update action loads existing content to preserve it when omitted, parses tags only when supplied, and delegates validated move/update semantics to Core.
Document list action routes empty or text output through paging and opens selected document content only for an interactive nonempty list.
Document view action distinguishes missing content, ambiguous IDs, plain/auto-plain output, and scrollable interactive rendering.
Collects every doctor diagnostic from config, duplicate repair preview, content/draft identity, and dependency graph before deciding whether to print success.
Makes --yes the sole noninteractive confirmation path and otherwise returns false for cancellation or declined repair without changing files.
Explains the three materially different reference states: no task groups, incomplete blocked scan, no references, or human-reviewable ambiguous references.
Determines Git versus filesystem-only initialization, refusing an unresolvable noninteractive no-repository case and confirming interactive intent.
Maps none, CLI, and MCP modes to their distinct output contracts, skipping MCP client setup noninteractively but retaining its summary.
Formats mode-specific summary lines so CLI instruction files, MCP server/setup state, and skipped integration are never conflated.
Restricts stdout/stderr error handling to EPIPE so an ordinary stream failure does not trigger an unrelated server shutdown path.
Board loader maps task status to a string and clears only milestones whose canonical keys are archived, preserving all other task data.
Defaults task-specific filters to task results and otherwise filters explicit type values with warnings for unsupported entries.
Validates ordinal and list flags before constructing the full create input, including aliases, draft status, optional milestone resolution, checklists, and DoD defaults intent.
Owns only post-validated persistence reporting: detailed plain output or concise ID/path output, with a single command-error conversion.
Composes scalar, checklist, label, list, and content parsers in an order that stops at the first user-visible validation error before buildTaskUpdateInput.
Serializes one plain task row from optional priority/type/status/due date and the shared acceptance-criteria progress suffix.
Formats one activity subsection with tagged/plain heading and truncation policy, selecting task rows when present or the supplied empty state when absent.
Runs the benchmark transaction: parses options, creates corpus, executes each surface cold/warm, builds report metadata/parity, prints chosen output, and removes the temporary root in finally.
Combines a captured operation failure and all cleanup failures after diagnostics are collected; it returns only for a clean run, uses cause for one failure, and AggregateError for many.
Polls a compiled browser server until deadline, immediately fails if process exited, returns only an OK response, retains last non-OK/network error, and sleeps between bounded fetches.
Normalizes task handling to clear/keep/reassign and rejects every other value before passing a typed removal request to the shared handler.
Combines output-mode validation and list-window parsing, then deliberately forces text when a paging window is requested from an interactive TTY.
Removes blank IDs and case/prefix-equivalent duplicates while retaining the first spelling for output and lookup diagnostics.
Registers the task command family and shares runtime output policy across create, list, edit, view, lifecycle, shorthand, and watch behavior.
Plain task-list page renderer selects its no-results message, priority header/rows, or status grouping after queryTaskList has performed all filtering.
Watch action validates JSON-only mode, watches the backlog/config paths, and returns a complete serialized list snapshot on each change.
Displays an age-qualified preview with at most five date-formatted task rows and returns a boolean that controls whether confirmation is meaningful.
Validates project config, configures Git operations, finds the configured terminal status, reports empty states, and enters the interactive age/confirmation flow only when tasks exist.
Provides key-specific recovery paths for milestone, DoD, configured collection, and immutable-prefix writes instead of a misleading generic set failure.
Document search action validates trimmed query length and limit before allocating search resources, filters document results, pages output, and disposes both stores.
Reports duplicate, missing-ID, and unreadable document/decision identities separately with the concrete remediation appropriate to each state.
Executes selected MCP client setup or guide opening and updates the corresponding instruction reminders before returning one setup summary.
Prompts repeatedly until a nonempty MCP client selection is made or cancellation explicitly aborts initialization.
Formats the advanced configuration block with colorized booleans, disabled padding, editor presence, and DoD defaults from the persisted result.
Instructions action chooses index versus a validated guide, emits actionable invalid-guide errors, and writes the selected normalized Markdown resource.
Browser action resolves project/configured port, starts a local server with open preference, registers shutdown handling, and delegates failures to runtime reporting.
Projects only task search results through loadTaskListItems while preserving the original mixed-result order and stopping safely if projection is short.
Formats task rows with status/priority and document or decision rows with their distinct payload identity, all sharing optional score rendering.
Applies the common clear/blank invariant independently to dependency aliases, replacement/add/remove references, and documentation flags.
Canonicalizes configured status case for grouping, retains unknown statuses, and orders configured groups before unknown ones without re-sorting their tasks.
Renders every status count with optional icon/tags and percentage, then always appends total/completion and conditionally Drafts. The branches encode display mode and draft presence.

Provides the initialization wizard state machine: status discovery preloads uninitialized defaults, next/back choose mode-specific steps with required-field validation, canProceed additionally validates custom relative paths, and toggle callbacks maintain selected client/instruction sets. Initialization submission is deliberately delegated to its returned initialize action.

Composes the task-list view around filters, server/local display selection, sortable rows, cleanup, and responsive fixed-column table layout. It derives status/priority/label/milestone options, maintains sort direction defaults, reports filter fetch errors, chooses empty versus table rendering, and synchronizes horizontal header/body scroll without feedback loops.

Coordinates board-level derived state rather than rendering each behavior itself: it normalizes filters and milestone aliases, builds lanes from all tasks including archival rules, derives visibility/collapse state, scopes selection to visible cards, and wires mutations, drag visibility, cleanup, metadata filters, loading/error state, and lane rendering together.

Owns the app shell's coherent data snapshot and refresh protocol. It maintains stable task/document/decision identities, canonicalizes/removes archived milestones on incoming task results, loads shell and search data in controlled phases, guards every async request by ID, tracks duplicate-repair state, and exposes task-only, milestone, full, reorder, and websocket-driven update paths.

clone_records.explanation: The apparent 12-line clone is the Core facade signature repeated by the delegated ProjectContentService method. Core passes identifier, title, autoCommit, and dueDate unchanged; ProjectContentService owns filesystem rename, optional commit, and compensating rollback. Extracting a shared signature would add an alias without removing behavior.

verification.no_remote_preflight: reported pass 3 and batch 10; retained test references are not execution proof
